target_customer: K-12 students and teachers, later schools and enterprises buying video lesson tools
problem: Students and teachers had trouble finding quality short video lessons and creating their own.
business_model: Free video lessons with paid supplemental tools such as Mini Courses, later enterprise licensing

founders.name: Ariel Braunstein
previous_startups: Pure Digital Technologies, maker of Flip Video (acquired by Cisco 2009)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2012 calls him co-founder of Pure Digital.

founders.name: Scott Kabat
founders.background_notes: Former marketing executive at Pure Digital per TechCrunch 2012.

competitors.name: Khan Academy
competitors.what: Free nonprofit library of video lessons

competitors.name: Educreations and ShowMe
competitors.what: Whiteboard apps for teachers competing with the Knowmia Teach iPad app

competitors.name: TED-Ed
competitors.what: Lets educators build lesson plans around TED video

technical_complexity.rationale: Video hosting, search and an iPad lesson recording app are standard engineering; the hard part was content supply and quality.

defensibility.rationale: Content was largely aggregated from YouTube and Vimeo plus teacher uploads, and Khan Academy was free, so copying the catalog approach was easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; TechSmith acquired the technology in 2014 and retired the product later.

market_need_then: Schools were adopting video learning and flipped classrooms and Khan Academy showed demand for video lessons; coverage in August 2012 framed Knowmia as a Khan Academy competitor.

branding.brand_signature: Pandora meets Yelp for K-12 videos positioning, and the Flip Video founders' reputation

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found no source on the name or logo; press attention rested on the founders' Flip Video history.

outcome_analysis: Knowmia was launched in August 2012 by Flip Video veterans to compete with free video lesson libraries. It was acquired by TechSmith in 2014 as a technology add-on, folded into TechSmith's learning products and later retired. Funding and traction are not public, so the quality of the exit is unknown.
notes: knowmia.com now redirects to a TechSmith page (not fetched). Acquisition date conflicts: one database says 2014-11-11, CB Insights says 2014-10, so only the year is recorded. CB Insights funding placeholders were unreliable and no seed round source was found. TechSmith retired the product (a school FAQ cites a July 13 shutdown, year unconfirmed). Education and prior roles beyond Pure Digital not found. Stage is Early per directory.
